body:
CURRENT MERGER PROCEDURE. Updated on Greg's direct request to Engram::Architect3 to put the rules in Engram memory. Sources: original Greg direction 2026-10-19 (retained in revision1); revised workflow recorded in rules-greg-merge-focus revision7, Advisor #2033/messageccf9fd6f, 2026-10-24T17:48:25Z. Later role/claim clarifications below are attributed operational interpretations, not new authority. Recover the current project's actual resume/STOP and the acting session's authority; this note does not resume stopped projects or authorize commit/push/install/restart by itself.

1. The Merger is non-authoring. A Coder (Sol/Opus under the current coding rule) implements, runs the new/focused tests, freezes the package and obtains required independent reviews. The package contains its base, patch/root/fingerprint, actual test results, complete review findings and finding disposition. Read full findings, not a compact "clean" label.
2. The Merger integrates an existing package onto current main/master. Under Greg's newer workflow, conflicts and product/test/documentation fixes return to a Coder, including one-line fixes. This supersedes revision1's wording that the Merger resolves conflicts. The Coder returns a corrected, tested and appropriately reviewed package with a new fingerprint. Never duplicate an already-landed package: verify Git ancestry and actual content.
3. Prepare dependencies and available disk in the actual integration root before allocating the full gate. Freeze the final tree and run one standard full gate on that tree. Reuse an existing complete PASS only for the identical final input with matching fingerprint evidence; a different final tree needs its own gate. A missing tool or unrun stage is not a product-test PASS. Existing run request/results, all required stage outcomes and fingerprint checks are the evidence; start messages and PIDs are not terminal outcomes.
4. Greg's recorded workflow removes host credit, acceptance evaluations and a second Merger-side review as extra conditions. Once the reviewed package and unchanged final tree meet the applicable tests and acting-session landing authority, proceed to check-in without an extra coordinator "go". Retain remote/base/fast-forward and exact-build requirements. Never infer rebase/force-push/restart authority. Source for this workflow is the Greg record cited above, not this note.
5. Work claims use supported native claim/recovery/handoff paths. Do not impersonate a removed holder or modify the store/clock to bypass WorkClaimHeld. Fable2 withdrew his inference that Greg's removal of credit/evaluation requirements also permitted ignoring a foreign live claim (mailbox-message-5bcdb64c-6bbc-4166-af97-86e61a9f1f42, 2026-10-25T03:44:26Z); no quoted Greg words addressed that exception. Claims themselves grant no filesystem/Git authority. The orphaned-claim recovery gap is tracked separately, not a reason to stall unrelated authorized packages.
6. Architect3's operational clarification, messagef12beda4 on 2026-10-25: a supported handoff of a separately held task need not wait for another task's full gate when it changes neither that gate's claim, source/root nor frozen input. Keep run attribution tied to its original task and fingerprint. The receiving Coder works in its own root under its own claim; preserve actual build limits and the single-full-gate rule. Do not invalidate or rerun a gate merely because unrelated tracker bookkeeping occurred when no integrity/input condition changed.
7. Use durable backend result wake where available (TermAl termal_resume_after_test_runs in the run's own project); record the run, owner, next action and recovery route. A failed wake never justifies rerunning tests. Unknown results are diagnosed from the existing run. Queue and package status live on tasks, not as a copied historic queue in permanent rules.
8. After completion the lander executes rules-post-completion-cleanup: explicit REMOVE/RETAIN decisions, preservation only for concrete active needs, and retirement of completed roots, unnecessary build outputs and safe stale local branches. This is post-completion responsibility, not another pre-landing gate.

These source-attributed updates supersede conflicting older summaries of the Merger's workflow within their stated scope. They do not rewrite AGENTS.md/CLAUDE.md, alter stored completion policies, or declare historic configuration values to be current host observations.
